entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8512"/><div sID="gen13843" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8512"/>20-22. The effect on the "remnant" (contrasted with the Assyrian remnant, <reference osisRef="Isa.10.19">Is 10:19</reference>); namely, those who shall be left after the invasion of Sennacherib, will be a return from dependence on external idolatrous nations, as Assyria and Egypt (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.18.21">2Ki 18:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Kgs.16.7-2Kgs.16.9">16:7-9</reference>), to the God of the theocracy; fulfilled in part in the pious Hezekiah's days; but from the future aspect under which Paul, in <reference osisRef="Rom.9.27">Ro 9:27</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rom.9.28">28</reference> (compare "short work" with "whole work," <reference osisRef="Isa.10.12">Is 10:12</reference>, here), regards the whole prophecy, the "remnant," "who stay upon the Lord," probably will receive their fullest realization in the portion of Jews left after that Antichrist shall have been overthrown, who shall "return" unto the Lord (<reference osisRef="Isa.6.13">Is 6:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.7.3">7:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.12.9">Zec 12:9</reference>, <reference osisRef="Zech.12.10">10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.14.2">14:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Zech.14.3">3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.12">Zep 3:12</reference>). <div eID="gen13843" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 20-22.
